feature1.prompt: The problem involves an inconsistent behavior in the conversion of world coordinates to pixel values in the sliced version of a 3D WCS, specifically within the SlicedLowLevelWCS implementation. When converting world coordinates on the full 3D WCS, the result is as expected, but slicing the WCS and converting only the spatial dimensions produces an erroneous value (essentially an infinite coordinate) for one of the dimensions. The goal is to fix the core logic in the conversion function so that the sliced WCS correctly computes the pixel values by dynamically accounting for the sliced world coordinates. After the fix, both unsliced and sliced conversions must yield consistent and accurate pixel positions.
feature1.hint_texts: Update the world_to_pixel_values method in the SlicedLowLevelWCS implementation so that instead of using a hard-coded constant (1.), the function computes and uses the proper sliced world coordinates. This involves introducing a new variable (sliced_out_world_coords) obtained via _pixel_to_world_values_all and then using its values when reconstructing the world_arrays_new for conversion.
feature1.entrypoint: File: astropy/wcs/wcsapi/wrappers/sliced_wcs.py; Function: world_to_pixel_values; Modification area: around the computation and use of sliced_out_world_coords (approximately lines 243-253).

feature2.prompt: A critical observation in the problem is that when a 3D WCS is sliced to form a 2D representation, the conversion from world coordinates to pixel coordinates does not behave as expected. In this sliced scenario, there is a failure in correctly handling the coupled dimensions, which leads to an abnormal pixel value in one of the spatial components. The objective of this feature is to introduce a validation mechanism that ensures the conversion in the sliced WCS properly reflects the spatial values, even when the spectral and spatial dimensions are coupled. The expected outcome is that after slicing, the transformation yields accurate spatial pixel positions consistent with those computed from the full 3D WCS.
feature2.hint_texts: Implement a new test case that simulates a coupled WCS scenario with a non-trivial PC matrix. The test should verify that the world_to_pixel conversion on the sliced WCS produces the correct spatial output. Ensure that the test clearly distinguishes between the misbehavior in the sliced conversion and the correct behavior expected after the fix.
feature2.entrypoint: File: astropy/wcs/wcsapi/wrappers/tests/test_sliced_wcs.py; add a new function to this file that defines the test for coupled world slicing, including the specification of the COUPLED_WCS_HEADER and the use of SlicedLowLevelWCS.

collaboration_points.shared_resources: Both features interact with the WCS and SlicedLowLevelWCS implementations in astropy/wcs/wcsapi. They share the same WCS header configurations and rely on the coordinate conversion APIs.
collaboration_points.integration_strategy: Feature1 must implement the correct conversion in world_to_pixel_values so that the sliced WCS returns expected pixel values. Feature2 will validate this behavior through a dedicated test. The integration relies on Feature1 exposing a robust interface that Feature2's test can accurately check.
collaboration_points.communication_needs: Developers on Feature1 and Feature2 need to coordinate on the expected behavior of the sliced world coordinate conversion. They should agree on the interpretation of the coupled spatial and spectral dimensions and ensure that the test case in Feature2 truly reflects the intended behavior of the fix in Feature1.
